messages:
maria: Quick design check — I'm proposing a small internal API change: collapse routing metadata + quota attribution into a single structured header (route-policy v3).

maria: Current pain: we have 3 headers (X-Route, X-Quota, X-Attrib) that SDKs parse separately and console mapping logic does repeated joins. v3 would be one payload to reduce ambiguity.

maria: Example candidate header:```X-Redwood-Route-Policy: version=3;route=us-west/low-latency;policy={"priority":10,"weights":{"model-a":0.7,"model-b":0.3}};quota=team:llm:project-xyz```

alex: fwiw, simpler surface sounds nice. main concern: breaking parsing in older SDKs that assume separate headers. we need a compatibility shim.

rui: SDK POV — we'll need to accept both forms for at least a full release cycle. For python/ts/go clients we can implement parsing that reads route-policy when present, else fallback to legacy headers. We should also emit a telemetry tag for which branch was used.

jamie: Console/telemetry — we'll want an explicit field in ingestion that indicates source format (legacy vs v3) so dashboards don't mix attribution logic. Also need to preserve per-token cost attribution until rollout completes.

maria: Agreed. Migration plan idea: 1) support both formats server-side + SDKs; 2) Console adds mapping flag to prefer v3 when present; 3) after N weeks, start warning headers in logs; 4) then deprecate legacy in 3 months. Thoughts?

alex: add a feature flag (console) so teams can opt into v3 early. Important for enterprise tenants.

rui: Implementation notes: parsing complexity increases because policy blob can contain nested json. We should standardize on URL-safe base64 for policy blob to avoid header-parsing issues. Example:```X-Redwood-Route-Policy: v=3;route=us-west;blob=eyJwcmlvcml0eSI6MTB9```

maria: Good call on base64. That avoids escaping headaches. Also we'll add a small checksum field so SDKs can detect truncated headers.

jamie: Dashboard impact — we'll need a migration dashboard tile listing requests using legacy vs v3, sample payloads, and a map of per-route cost. UX: add a toggle to let customers preview how their attribution will change.

sasha: Product note: require a migration playbook for customers on Dedicated/Private. They may have proxy rules that rewrite headers; we should surface recommended envoy snippets.

rui: SDK release plan: publish non-breaking minor SDKs with v3 parse and telemetry opt-in, coordinate deprecation warnings printed by SDKs when legacy headers seen, then bump major only when we remove legacy.

alex: Ops question: what about rate-limiting bucket changes? If quota attribution switches shape, quota ledgers must accept both keys. We need a compatibility layer in the metering service.

maria: I'll open a metering PR to accept both `team:llm:...` and the new `quota` KV. Also will attach schema examples.

ops-bot: deploy:route-policy-v3-proposal created by maria — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/proposals/route-policy-v3

jamie: Telemetry detail: add a boolean field `route_policy_source` in ingestion events (values: legacy, v3, shim) and include SDK version. That will let us detect if a client naive-parsed the blob.

rui: One more SDK detail — Go client uses header canonicalization that lowercases keys; ensure server accepts both canonical forms and that blob isn't mangled. We'll add unit tests.

alex: timeline proposal: experiment behind FF for 2 weeks; then opt-in via console for customers; release SDKs in week-3; warn in logs week-6; full enforcement week-12.

maria: timeline noted. I'll draft RFC with FF flags and console tile mocks. Who can help with envoy examples? sasha?

sasha: Yep — I'll prepare envoy snippets and add a slide for the customer playbook.

rui: I'll coordinate the SDK changelogs and prepare backwards-compatible parsers for py/ts/go.

jamie: I'll mock the dashboard tile and ingestion schema and work with infra to add the `route_policy_source` field.

maria: Thanks. Action items: maria -> RFC + metering PR; sasha -> envoy snippets + playbook; rui -> SDK patches + tests; jamie -> telemetry + dashboard tile; alex -> coordinate FF rollout with infra.

alex: ack. Ping me once RFC merged and I'll open the infra work item for the FF gating.

maria: Will do. Short follow-up: should we require signed header checksum for v3 from the start, or add later? Prefer added from start to avoid malformed-attribution issues.

rui: Prefer start. SDKs can verify and emit a `route_policy_checksum` tag.

jamie: agreed. makes debugging easier.

sasha: ok from product side.

maria: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link once it's up.
